The Oslo Postdoctoral Research Fellowship 2026 offers an exceptional opportunity for early-career researchers to investigate children’s and young people’s digital lives at the University of Oslo. Hosted by the Department of Media and Communication, this fully funded 4-year position is affiliated with the Centre for Studies of Children, Youth, and Media and the EU Kids Online Norway network, enabling independent, policy-relevant research.

The University of Oslo (UiO) is Norway’s oldest and highest-ranked university, renowned for its strong research environment in the social sciences and humanities. The Department of Media and Communication is a leading center for media studies in Scandinavia, with particular expertise in children, youth, and media research. The EU Kids Online network is an internationally recognized collaborative research initiative.

Oslo Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Benefits

  • Fully funded 4-year postdoctoral appointment.
  • Competitive salary and employee benefits according to Norwegian regulations.
  • Opportunity to conduct independent research.
  • Access to national and international EU Kids Online datasets (where relevant and approved).
  • International collaboration with leading researchers.
  • Career development plan and academic mentoring.
  • Teaching experience and pedagogical training.
  • Opportunities to publish internationally and build a strong academic profile.

Oslo Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Eligibility Criteria

  • A PhD (or equivalent) in Media and Communication, Sociology, Psychology, Education, Childhood Studies, or another relevant discipline.
  • A research proposal closely connected to the EU Kids Online Norway project.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Strong motivation and suitability for independent academic research.
  • Experience researching children, youth, and digital technologies (preferred).
  • Expertise in qualitative, quantitative, mixed, or digital research methods (preferred).
  • International or interdisciplinary research collaboration experience (preferred).
  • Teaching experience (preferred).

How to Apply for Oslo Postdoctoral Research Fellowship

  • Visit the official University of Oslo job portal.
  • Carefully review the eligibility requirements.
  • Prepare a research proposal aligned with EU Kids Online Norway.
  • Upload all required documents.
  • Submit your application before 15 August 2026.
Apply on the official website

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Here are some frequently asked questions about the Oslo Postdoctoral Research Fellowship 2026, covering eligibility, benefits, application process, and more.

What is the University of Oslo Postdoctoral Research Fellowship?

It is a fully funded 4-year postdoctoral research position at the University of Oslo’s Department of Media and Communication, focusing on children, youth, and digital media. Fellows conduct independent, policy-relevant research within the EU Kids Online Norway network.

Who can apply for this postdoctoral fellowship?

Applicants must hold a PhD in Media and Communication, Sociology, Psychology, Education, Childhood Studies, or a related discipline. A research proposal closely connected to the EU Kids Online Norway project is required, along with excellent English skills.

What are the benefits of the fellowship?

The fellowship provides a competitive salary, employee benefits, independent research opportunity, access to EU Kids Online datasets, collaboration with international experts, a career development plan, teaching experience, and pedagogical training.

What research areas are acceptable for the proposal?

Proposals can cover children’s digital media use, online safety, digital rights, digital literacy, media regulation, wellbeing, social media and young people, comparative international studies, digital technologies and childhood, or media and communication research.

How long is the fellowship?

The appointment lasts four years. The fellow will dedicate 75% of the time to independent research and 25% to teaching and administrative duties, gaining both research and pedagogical experience.

What documents are required for the application?

Applicants must submit an online application, CV, research proposal, list of publications, copies of academic certificates and transcripts, the PhD dissertation or documentation of submission, and any other supporting documents requested by the university.

When is the application deadline?

The deadline to submit applications is 15 August 2026. All materials must be uploaded online through the official job portal before that date.

Is the fellowship fully funded?

Yes, the position is fully funded. It includes a competitive salary and employee benefits in accordance with Norwegian regulations, covering all research and living costs for the duration of the fellowship.

Do I need to be a Norwegian citizen to apply?

No, the fellowship is open to all nationalities. The University of Oslo welcomes international applicants who meet the academic and research proposal requirements.

How do I submit my application?

Applications are submitted online via the official University of Oslo job portal. The direct link can be found on the official announcement page. Make sure all required documents are uploaded before the deadline.
